Study 1 of Rogoza et al. (2024) is the INITIAL 30-item adjective pool of the Narcissistic Antagonism Scale, not the published 18-item NAS: the paper's Study 1 removes megalomaniac, egoistic, egocentric, aggressive, boastful and domineering. instrument is named accordingly. Response points 2-6 are unlabelled in the source (only 1 = Not at all and 7 = Extremely are anchored), so their option_text is left blank rather than padded with the number. item_text is the adjective as capitalised in the Study 1 codebook; the IRW item code is the same adjective lowercased, so item_text carries no information the code does not already carry.

Not a defect, recorded because the table name invites the wrong reading: this is the 18-item Study 2 NAS item POOL, not the published 16-item NAS. Study 1 reduced an initial 30-adjective pool to 18; Study 2 administered those 18 alongside the NVS (11) and NGS (13) and dropped two more (NAS17 Condescending and NAS18 Selfish, which cross-loaded onto the neurotic factor) to reach the final 16-item NAS. So NAS1..NAS16 are the published scale in its published order and NAS17/NAS18 are pool items that did not survive.

The instrument's response scale labels only its endpoints (1 = Not at all, 7 = Extremely). option_text is blank for resp 2-6 by design; the source publishes no wording for those points and they were not padded with their own numbers.

The `instructions` text is the Study 2 Codebook's single instruction for the consolidated 42-adjective pool that also contains the NVS and NGS items, so the same instruction legitimately applies to the sibling tables nas_rogoza_2024_study2_nvs and nas_rogoza_2024_study2_ngs (neither owned nor written by this run). The codebook heads it 'Adjective Scales of Narcissism'; `instrument` names the NAS specifically because that is what this table holds.
